name: North Carolina
overview: North Carolina’s named circuit breaker is a tax deferral with repayment conditions. Separate elderly/disabled and disabled-veteran exclusions reduce taxable value.

programs.name: Circuit Breaker Tax Deferment Program
programs.ageRule: Age 65+ or qualifying total permanent disability.
programs.incomeDefinition: Prior-calendar-year income under the statutory property-tax relief definition.
programs.incomeLimits: No more than 150% of the annually adjusted elderly/disabled exclusion limit; use 2025 AV-9.
programs.maximumBenefit: Eligible tax above 4% or 5% of income is deferred, not forgiven outright.
programs.formulaSummary: Cap current qualifying tax payment at the applicable income percentage and defer the balance; statutory events can trigger repayment of deferred taxes and interest.
programs.application: Apply annually to the county tax assessor using AV-9.
eligibilityNotes: At least five consecutive years of ownership and permanent-residence occupancy are generally required.
interactions: Cannot combine with the elderly/disabled or disabled-veteran exclusion.

programs.name: Elderly or Disabled Exclusion
programs.ageRule: Age 65+ or qualifying total permanent disability.
programs.maximumBenefit: Greater of $25,000 or 50% of eligible appraised residence value.
programs.formulaSummary: Exclude the statutory portion of permanent-residence value from taxation.
programs.application: AV-9 to county assessor, generally by June 1.
interactions: Only one of the three AV-9 relief programs may benefit each owner.

programs.name: Real estate tax itemized deduction
programs.incomeDefinition: Federal income rules affect the itemized deduction.
programs.incomeLimits: Income rules affect larger itemized deductions.
programs.maximumBenefit: Claim the qualified amount within the applicable itemized deduction limits.
programs.formulaSummary: Add qualifying mortgage interest and real estate taxes after the federal limits. Apply the $20,000 North Carolina combined limit.
programs.application: Claim on D-400 Schedule A when you itemize on your North Carolina return.
eligibilityNotes: Use qualified real estate taxes for the applicable form.
interactions: The $20,000 limit applies to the combined qualified mortgage interest and real estate tax deduction.

sources.title: N.C. Department of Revenue, conformity update question 16

researchNotes: The circuit breaker defers property-tax liabilities, with repayment under the statutory triggers.
The linked relief application does not establish a statewide renter credit.
